{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
I spent three months developing a new customer retention algorithm. When it reduced churn by 15%, my director presented it to the executives as 'something the team put together,' then accepted a bonus and promotion. My name was never mentioned. He knew exactly whose work it was.

CANDIDATE A:
In fourth grade, I designed a science-fair experiment on plant growth. My teacher later submitted the project to a district teaching competition as an example of an experiment she had created. She removed my name, accepted the award personally, and used it in her promotion application. I watched from the audience while she described 'her' project.

CANDIDATE B:
I developed a customer retention algorithm over three months. My director presented it to executives and made sure to highlight my contribution by name. I was invited to the meeting, recognized in front of leadership, and received a spot bonus for the work.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:4"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both stories involve an individual who puts in significant effort and creativity, only to have their work appropriated by someone in a position of authority who takes credit for it."}
